waivedCriteria.why: The clause is expressed as a list of forbidden OBS input kinds and asserts that the harness reads only windows it launched. gdigrab reads the composited desktop by construction, so the MECHANISM clause cannot be met -- and cannot be met by ANY backend that draws a cursor, because the cursor is composited by the desktop. That is the same fact that stops OBS's WGC from ever showing one.

notWaived.note: Structural: -an on the command line, no audio device in the graph, and ffprobe reads back zero audio streams on all 11 recordings. This is the clause OBS could NOT satisfy -- it muxes a silent track regardless of configuration (Session 4 measured 1 audio track on all 11 of its recordings).
One rectangle, one video stream, no compositing.
All met at the full bar: 10 of 10 clean runs, 11 measured, 1 excluded as control-contaminated. Nothing in C1-C6 is waived.

attestation: I accept ffmpeg gdigrab as the cursor-capable capture backend for Set 113's tutorial recordings, waiving ONLY C7's mechanism clause ('never captures the screen'). The clause's stated PURPOSE -- never capture the operator's webcam, microphone or whole screen -- is met and measured: no camera, microphone or audio device is opened at any point, no monitor-wide frame is ever written to disk, the captured rectangle is the target window's client area, and an occlusion guard refuses to start and aborts mid-capture when anything unrelated enters that rectangle (measured to catch a 25.39% leak that would otherwise reach the frame). I accept the trade this makes explicit: availability for safety -- on a busy desktop this backend will refuse to record where OBS would have recorded cleanly. This waiver is NARROW. It does not waive C1-C6, it does not waive C7's no-audio or single-source clauses, it does not apply to the OBS backend (whose Session 4 verdict stands at FAIL on C2 and C7), and it does not license capturing anything other than a single bounded application window. Every recording made under it still owes the Session 7 publication safety pass, per video, before anything leaves the machine.
